sources.citation: The 12 V 7 Ah valve-regulated lead-acid (VRLA, AGM) monobloc, a common alarm and UPS battery class: six 2 V cells (12 V nominal), 7 Ah at the 20-hour rate, case about 151 × 65 × 94 mm and 98 mm to the terminal tops. Typical of published manufacturer datasheets for the class, paraphrased; not one vendor's values. The size is the footprint on the bench (151 × 65 mm) and the height above it (98 mm).

A rested lead-acid cell's open-circuit voltage is roughly its electrolyte's specific gravity plus 0.84 V. For a VRLA monobloc at 25 °C, published state-of-charge charts give about 12.9 V (2.15 V per cell) at full charge and about 11.8 V (1.97 V per cell) fully discharged. Paraphrased from the lead-acid chapters of Linden's Handbook of Batteries (T. B. Reddy, ed., 4th ed., McGraw-Hill, 2011) and VRLA manufacturers' charts.

Internal resistance of a fully charged 12 V 7 Ah VRLA battery at 25 °C: about 23 mΩ, mid-range of the class's published datasheets (roughly 17 to 28 mΩ). Those figures are usually 1 kHz AC tester readings, which read lower than the DC resistance a step load sees; F2.4 records using the AC figure as a DC internal resistance as an abstraction.
game-design: the two terminals sit on the top of the case, 115 mm apart, chosen for drawing leads; not modelled on a product.
